intent: The message a Combobox's popup shows when no item matches the typed query, announced politely to assistive technology.
typical_uses: A short no-results line beside the list

dont_use_when.situation: A page or panel with no data to show at all

invariants.text: The element is always rendered, and its children only while the root's filtered items are empty; that result exists only when the root has `items`, so without `items` the message shows at all times.
The element is a polite, atomic live region (role "status", `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic`), so assistive technology announces the message when it appears.

anti_patterns.dont: Mount ComboboxEmpty conditionally, or hide it with `hidden` or a display of none
anti_patterns.do_instead: Render it unconditionally and let it decide when to show its children; a live region that is not in the DOM before its text arrives is not announced reliably

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the message's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the message's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (empty for this part). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A no-results line beside the list

bad.title: The message shown only when the caller decides
bad.why: ComboboxEmpty already shows its children only while nothing matches; mounting it conditionally drops the live region the announcement needs.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ComboboxEmptyState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the message's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ComboboxEmptyState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the message's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (empty for this part). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.
